## Purpose

[backend/alembic/env.py](../../backend/alembic/env.py) is the Alembic migration environment: it resolves the database URL,
registers the SQLAlchemy metadata Alembic diffs against, and runs migrations in either offline
(emit-SQL) or online (live-connection) mode.

Every `alembic revision --autogenerate` and `alembic upgrade` invocation — plus
[backend/init_db.py](../../backend/init_db.py)'s programmatic call — goes through this file.

## Shape

- Puts `backend/` on `sys.path` so `app.*` is importable regardless of the invoking CWD.
- Imports `app.core.config.settings` and `app.models.database.Base`, plus `app.models` itself
  purely for its import side effect: importing the package registers every model class onto
  `Base.metadata`, which is what makes `target_metadata = Base.metadata` complete enough for
  autogenerate to see all tables.
- Resolves the DB URL with a fixed precedence: an already-set `sqlalchemy.url` on the `Config`
  (the path tests use, building a `Config` and calling `upgrade()` programmatically) wins over
  `settings.DATABASE_URL` (the runtime/production path); `alembic.ini`'s own `sqlalchemy.url`
  slot is deliberately left blank so it can never silently supply a stale URL.
- `run_migrations_offline()` / `run_migrations_online()` both pass `compare_type=True` and
  `compare_server_default=True` to `context.configure`, plus a `_render_item` extension-point
  stub (currently a no-op that always falls back to Alembic's default rendering).
- `run_migrations_online()` reuses a connection from `config.attributes["connection"]` if the
  caller already attached one (tests / multi-migration transactions), else builds a fresh engine
  with `NullPool`.

## Why this shape

**Single source of truth for the DB URL**: dev and prod must resolve it identically to the
FastAPI app (`settings.DATABASE_URL`) rather than a hardcoded `alembic.ini` value that could
drift.

`compare_type`/`compare_server_default` are turned on because Alembic's default autogenerate
only diffs the *set* of columns, not their type or default — without these flags a column-type
change (e.g. widening a `String(50)` to `String(255)`) would silently produce an empty
migration.

The connection-reuse branch in `run_migrations_online()` exists specifically so tests can run
multiple migrations inside one transaction without Alembic opening its own connection each
time.
